biography: Alexandre Garcia's journey began in the dusty backroads of Minas Gerais, Brazil, far from the glitz of international circuits. His first taste of speed came behind the wheel of his grandfather's battered pickup truck, navigating treacherous dirt tracks delivering supplies to remote farms. It was there, amidst the red dust and unforgiving terrain, that he honed his raw talent. A local dirt racing competition at 16 was the turning point; driving a borrowed, barely-functional buggy, Garcia stunned seasoned veterans with his fearless overtaking maneuvers and uncanny ability to read the changing track conditions. This victory earned him a spot in Formula Dirt, a regional racing series. While he's shown promise with several podium finishes, Garcia is still finding his footing, transitioning from raw talent to refined skill in a highly competitive environment. Currently, he's focused on consistency and securing more sponsorship to climb the ranks.
drivingStyle: Garcia's driving style is characterized by calculated aggression. He's not one for flamboyant, high-risk moves in the early stages of a race. Instead, he prefers to study his opponents, identify their weaknesses, and exploit them with precise, late-braking overtakes. Tire management is a strength, as he conserves his rubber early on, allowing him to push harder in the closing laps. He remains remarkably calm under pressure, a trait often attributed to his upbringing in the demanding environment of rural Brazil.

careerHighlight: Winning the 2021 Copa do Brasil de Dirt Rally, a national championship event, against all odds after starting from the back of the grid due to a mechanical failure in qualifying.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2023 São Paulo Grand Prix due to a mechanical failure, costing him a guaranteed victory and valuable championship points.
